documents.title: DOC 45 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - left the track and gained lasting advantage
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 4 - left the track and gained lasting advantage

details.fact: Car 4 (Herta) cut the chicane at Turn 7 and gained lasting advantage over Car 15 (Dunne).
details.infringement: Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
details.reason: The Stewards examined video evidence. Approaching Turn 6 Car 15 attempted an inside pass on Car 4. Car 15 was alongside prior to and at the apex of Turn 6, then Car 4 went wide and off the track and rejoined after Turn 7 ahead of Car 15. To have the rights for a turn the car who is trying to overtake on the inside has to have its front axle at least alongside the mirror of the other car prior to and at the apex, and in this case Car 15 earned the rights for the turn. The Stewards considered that Car 4 went off track at Turn 7 and after rejoining the track gained a position over Car 15. The Stewards, having analysed extensively the matter, under these circumstances considered that failing to lose an advantage constitutes gaining an advantage. Therefore the Stewards elect to impose the standard penalty for leaving the track and gaining a lasting advantage.

documents.title: DOC 44 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - failure to comply with RD Instructions - tyres laid flat
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 16 - failure to comply with RD Instructions - tyres laid flat

details.fact: During the mandatory pit stop for Car 16, the front left tyre rolled away, rather than being placed immediately flat.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 42) and heard the team representative. They examined video evidence. The team representative admitted that the left front tyre of Car 16 rocked momentarily during the tyre change. Video evidence confirmed that the left tyre of Car 16 rolled in the working area for Car 16. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that during the pit stop of Car 16 (Maini), the left front tyre removed from the car was not placed flat on the ground in a stable condition by an ART Grand Prix team member. Consequently, the tyre rolled away from the pit stop position before coming to rest. This was contrary to Item 2(iii) of the Race Director Competition Notes – Tyres and Pit Stop Procedures, which requires tyres removed from cars during pit stops to be placed flat on the ground in a stable condition. The standard fine is assessed and the team is reminded of the safety issues that can result from tyres not being placed flat and securely in the pit lane.

documents.title: DOC 43 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Rodin Motorsport - unsafe act in pit lane
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Rodin Motorsport - unsafe act in pit lane

details.fact: An operational team member crossed the live pit lane during the Reconnaissance Lap in front of Car 12.
details.infringement: Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: A fine of 500 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the FIA.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Document 41) and heard the team representative. They examined video evidence. During the starting procedure, an engineer from Rodin Motorsport started to run late from Pit wall to pit lane while cars were going through the fast lane. This is not compliant with the regulations of 2026 FIA International Sporting Code, by creating unsafe situation on the pit lane for competitors and team representatives. During the hearing, the Team Manager admitted the mistake. Therefore, in keeping with the previous decision made, the Stewards decided to impose a fine to the team.

documents.title: DOC 32 - 2026 Budapest Event - DECISION - Car 5 - allegedly forcing another car off track
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 5 - allegedly forcing another car off track

details.fact: Car 5 (Leon) allegedly forced Car 2 (Durksen) off track at Turn 2.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 27 & 28) and heard the Drivers of Car 5 (Leon) and Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence. The Driver of Car 2 explained that on the approach to Turn 2 he was ahead, as well as at the apex and at the exit where he had earned priority pursuant to the Driving Standard Guidelines. He said that Car 5 did not provide him with room on the exit as a result of which he was forced off the track to the right and Car 5 remained in front of him. The Driver of Car 5 acknowledged that he managed Turn 2 to try an inside overtaking manoeuvre on Car 2 by getting the rights for the corner, but said that Car 2 had not earned priority in accordance with the Driving Standard Guidelines and that he regained priority. After analysing the matter extensively, the Stewards are not sufficiently satisfied that Car 5 forced Car 2 off the track at the exit of Turn 2, therefore elected take no further action.

documents.title: DOC 31 - 2026 Budapest Event - INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - causing a collision
documents.subject: INFRINGEMENT - Car 6 - causing a collision

details.fact: Car 6 (Tsolov) made contact with Car 11 (Montoya) at Turn 1.
details.infringement: Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
details.decision: Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4 points. As Car 6 was not classified and the penalty could not be served during the race, it was converted to a 5 place grid drop for the next race in which the Driver participates.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 25 & 26) and heard the Drivers of Car 6 (Tsolov) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video evidence, on board footage and GPS data. The driver of Car 6 explained that he had DRS and saw an opportunity to overtake Car 11 on the inside of Turn 1. He stated that, upon reaching the apex, Car 11 moved towards the right hand side of the track, leaving insufficient room and resulting in contact between the two cars. The driver of Car 11 explained that he approached and negotiated the corner normally and observed Car 6 attempting a late overtaking manoeuvre. He acknowledged that Car 6 had achieved overlap at the apex but contended that this was a consequence of Car 6 carrying excessive speed into Turn 1, which forced him to drive on the kerb. Contact subsequently occurred between the cars during the corner. Having carefully considered the matter, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was overly optimistic in attempting the overtake at Turn 1. The manoeuvre was initiated late, and Car 6 carried excessive speed into the corner, which significantly contributed to the incident. The Stewards concluded that Car 6 was predominantly responsible for the collision and therefore elected to impose a drop of five grid positions for the drivers’ next race plus 2 penalty points.

documents.title: DOC 15 - 2026 Budapest Event - DECISION - Car 14 - alleged impeding of Car 11 at Turn 12 in Qualifying
documents.subject: DECISION - Car 14 - alleged impeding of Car 11 at Turn 12 in Qualifying

details.fact: Car 14 (Stenshorne) allegedly impeded Car 11 (Montoya) at Turn 12.
details.infringement: Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
details.reason: The Stewards summoned (Documents 13 & 14) and heard the Drivers of Car 14 (Stenshorne) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video and marshalling sector times. The driver of Car 14 explained that both cars were on a warm-up lap and that he was attempting to create a gap ahead in preparation for his push lap. The driver of Car 11 agreed that both cars were on a warm-up lap but acknowledged that he was attempting to overtake Car 14 in order to secure a more favourable track position for his push lap. Marshalling sector times confirmed that both cars were running in sequence and were on warm-up laps at the time of the incident. Accordingly, the Stewards determined that Car 14 did not unnecessarily impede Car 11 and therefore decided that no further action was warranted.
